prompt_hack.title: The 'Checkpoint Resume' Pattern — Survive Session Crashes on Long Tasks
steps: Problem: Long-running agent tasks (builds, migrations, multi-step workflows) lose all progress if a session crashes, times out, or gets interrupted.
Create a checkpoint file at each major step: write progress to a known path (e.g., /tmp/task-checkpoint.json) with current step, completed items, and next action.
Add to AGENTS.md: 'Before starting any multi-step task, check for existing checkpoint files. If found, resume from the last checkpoint instead of restarting.'
This pattern pairs with Task Supervisor (edition #10) and is exactly how the Daily Claw pipeline survives cron interruptions.
prompt_hack.why_it_matters: As agents take on longer autonomous tasks (cron jobs, backlog work, multi-file edits), resilience matters more than speed. A 2-hour task that crashes at step 6 of 7 and has to restart is worse than a 3-hour task that can resume from any point. Build for recovery, not just execution.

community_build.title: The China Agent Stack Is Real — And It's Complete
community_build.description: In the span of one week, China assembled a full agent ecosystem: Tencent shipped WorkBuddy (workplace agent), Xiaomi's MiClaw entered closed beta (mobile agent), Nano Labs announced ClawPC (dedicated hardware), Shenzhen committed government grants (fiscal policy), and now Bloomberg reports Chinese tech stocks are surging on the thesis. Hardware + software + mobile + policy + capital — all in one week. No other country has this level of coordinated agent infrastructure buildout.
community_build.how_to_replicate: You can't replicate government policy, but the playbook is instructive: build on top of OpenClaw (don't compete with it), target specific verticals (workplace, mobile, hardware), and move fast. For individual builders: the AKShare CN Market skill and Tencent's WorkBuddy API docs are the starting points if you want to build for the Chinese agent market.
